content.text: Given my infamously early wake-up time and disciplined schedule, a lot of people have asked for my daily routine and the rationale behind it over the years!
This is basically how my broader
Personal Systems

translate into what I actually do every day. Definitely a living doc, definitely not a schedule I follow perfectly, and always changing as I find ways to improve it! Hope you find something useful! For how I work with other people, check out my
Personal Operating Manual

Growing up, I was very definitively a night owl. It wasn’t until cutting for my first bodybuilding competition in 2022 when my hormones got thrown completely out of whack that I started naturally / uncontrollably waking up at 4am, 3am, and sometimes even 2am wired 😅. Ever since mid-2022, I made the permanent transition to that earlier time and haven’t looked back!
Why wake up extremely early? Here are a few of my favorites:
It’s easy, actually

It doesn’t really take any extraordinary willpower to wake up early! Fundamentally, I’m still sleeping the same amount as anyone else would, I’m just shifting my schedule earlier. Commit to it for a couple of weeks and watch your circadian rhythm naturally shift!
I get 4+ hours completely to myself
That give me time to grab full control of my schedule before anyone can disturb me!
I try to allocate as much of this time as I can to “eating the frog” – working on the day’s biggest and most important project
Once the meetings + comms bombardment starts, my plate gets filled up will small yet urgent tasks which can easily engulf the rest of my day
I can’t miss a workout
When I work out this early in the morning before all meeting, it’s nearly impossible to make an excuse to miss it (not that working out too little is ever an issue 😅)
I only have to shower once
There are naturally two points where I have to shower daily: once after my workout and once before my meetings. Why not line the two up?!
I have enough time
This gives me enough time to work out early in the morning, shower, and get going
My benchmark is at least 4 hours between waking and first meeting. That’s the minimum I can fit my full morning routine into and not feel too rushed
I naturally out-work everyone
By starting work before 4am every morning, most people’s 9-5 becomes my 12-hour work day. The inertia naturally becomes that I out-work everyone!

title.text: Why do I lift in the morning?

content.text: I can consume as much caffeine as I want! As opposed to working out in the afternoon where I have to be weary about consuming too much caffeine and not being able to sleep at night.
Caffeine consumed while fasting and shortly after waking hits like no other!
The morning endorphins propels me through the rest of the day
I have to shower before my morning meetings. If I don’t work out then as well, that means I have to shower twice a day. Instead, I can stack the two together and save myself a bunch of time!
I usually have the gym all to myself which means I can use whatever equipment I want!
The gym is a great mental break / escape / transition point. Good time to switch gears in the morning after some deep work
Note: I definitely am sacrificing ~10% strength + intensity in the gym
Return to work! This is some of my most productive time of the day as I have endorphins flowing and dawn is just starting to break

Taken from
Why We Sleep
, here’s how alertness naturally varies throughout the day:
Given this, you could argue that alertness follows a sawtooth pattern throughout the day. However, I think most people actually experience a sinusoidal pattern of alertness.
Finally, most people would probably tell you they desire a square-wave pattern of alertness if it were reasonably achievable.
Here’s my best attempt at doing so!
AM
: Get the blood flowing, caffeine + ⍺-GPC, and artificial sun exposure ASAP
PM
: Sleep stack + melatonin (and a whole routine in general) to prime the body for sleep
Make this your #1 priority!
Despite popular opinion, caffeine is actually a
very safe drug
with tons of benefits and very few risks. As such, I’ve grown much more liberal with my intake of caffeine over the past few years.
The biggest “
risk”
of caffeine is

reduced sleep quality. This is definitely something I want to minimize. Analyzing my own average caffeine consumption throughout the day (see the sawtooth graph below), I go to sleep on approximately 110mg of caffeine. Obviously not ideal but 🤷‍♂️ . (

I take a bunch of supplements every morning and evening to improve various aspects of my life.
Examine.com
is my favorite site for determining the efficacy of various supplements! This is how I originally curated my stacks in 2022.
Because I also eat a
highly
restrictive diet, I take a greens blend (eg. Athletic Greens) and a daily men’s multivitamin. The efficacy of both of these are mixed so I view these more as insurance policies than anything.
Contrarian opinion: I think most people actually get
too much
sleep!
Yes, I’ve read
Why We Sleep
which makes a statistically rigorous argument for 8+ hours daily. However, studies also show that anywhere between 6-8 hours works. In fact, all cause mortality with 8 hours is actually
higher
than with 5 hours: (caveat: correlation vs causation). Also, my father was a lifelong 4-6hrs/night sleeper so I might’ve
inherited the gene from him
When I oversleep, I often feel
more
lethargic the following day yet have trouble going to sleep at the end of the night.
I’ve found the right amount of sleep for me varies from anywhere between 5 hours and 7.5 hours (avg. 6.25h) per night depending on weight, exercise, season, etc.!

Why does the amount of sleep I need change depending on how much I weigh / whether I'm actively gaining or losing weight / the season? I'm a bodybuilder who bulks and cuts 20+ pounds per year, peaking in Jan (when I need the most sleep at 7+ hours) and at my lowest in the summer (when I only need like 5.5h)
Your changing sleep needs are influenced by a combination of physiological, metabolic, and environmental factors related to your bodybuilding routines and seasonal rhythms. Here’s why:
After travel, an outstanding weekend, or something else that kicks me off my normal routine, I’ve developed a simple strategy to get back on track.
My top priority is always to get back to my normal sleep schedule. In fact, I’ve even done 12-hour schedule flips (US ↔ India) without any jet lag whatsoever.
How? Using supplements to modulate alertness: caffeine as an extender, the sleep stack with melatonin as a light switch.
Take the time to learn how your body reacts to both and how you can then use them as tools to get back on track after disruption!
For me, I find that once I get back into my normal sleep routine and have those first 4 hours in the morning to grab full control of my schedule that the rest falls back into place rather quickly 😄
